children: Oil futures were mixed at midday Thursday after fresh U.S.-Iran strikes rekindled fears of prolonged disruptions to Middle East oil flows.

As of noon ET, the October West Texas Intermediate contract rose 13cts to $91.09/bbl, while November WTI fell 43cts to $87.85/bbl. November ICE Brent crude dropped 19cts to $95.44/bbl, with the December contract trading 56cts lower at $91.51/bbl.

Crude benchmarks earlier reached six-week intraday highs, with Brent briefly topping $97/bbl. The benchmarks were on track for a fourth consecutive session of gains and had risen more than 10% on the week before pulling back from their highs.

Refined product futures were mixed. October RBOB traded 0.01ct higher at $3.1040/gal, with November down 0.25ct at $2.9357/gal. Meanwhile, the October ULSD contract fell 7.63cts to $4.6059/gal, with November trading 6.32cts lower at $4.4319/gal.

The latest hostilities in the Middle East included fresh U.S. strikes across Iran, Kuwait's interception of incoming Iranian missiles and drones, and threats from Israel's Minister of Defense Israel Katz to target Iranian energy infrastructure. The Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is extending troop deployments in the region.

Supply concerns are in focus as vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains below average. Iran has also expanded its list of non-compliant vessels subject to fines, confiscation or detention if they attempt to transit the strait.

Ritterbusch & Associates said Thursday that some comfort had emerged as more ships were reportedly exiting the Strait of Hormuz — but that a diplomatic resolution still appeared distant. The consulting firm said the conflict could keep petroleum prices elevated through year-end.
